trump-00-matto.name: The Fool
trump-00-matto.Scene: Il Matto (The Fool) of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows the wandering jester figure — a ragged or motley-dressed figure in comic or disheveled attire, carrying a staff or bundle, with a dog or animal nipping at him. The Matto is the unnumbered outsider of the trump sequence, equivalent to the Marseille Mat and the standard tarot Fool. In the Minchiate tradition, the Matto stands outside the numbered sequence of 40 trumps, a wild card that is neither highest nor lowest but rather apart from the hierarchy entirely.

trump-01-papa-1.name: 1 — Papa One (Il Bagatto · the Juggler / “Trivial Performer”)
trump-01-papa-1.Scene: Papa Uno (Pope One) is the first of the five Papi — the Minchiate's most distinctive innovation, replacing the Papess, Pope, Emperor, Empress, and Lovers of the standard tarot with a sequence of five pope or emperor figures. In the Minchiate, the Papi are the lowest-ranking trumps (I-V), the figures of ecclesiastical and imperial authority placed at the base of the trump hierarchy rather than in the middle. Papa Uno is the first and weakest pope, his vestments less elaborate than those of the higher Papi, in the 19th-century Florentine engraving style of this 1860-1890 edition.

trump-02-papa-2.name: 2 — Papa Two (the Grand Duke)
trump-02-papa-2.Scene: Papa Due (Pope Two) is the second of the five Papi in the Minchiate Fiorentina — another papal or imperial figure in vestments and regalia, slightly more elaborate or more prominent than Papa Uno in the trump hierarchy. The five Papi form a unique sequence at the base of the Minchiate's 40 trumps, a quintet of authority figures not found in any other tarot tradition.

trump-03-papa-3.name: 3 — Papa Three (the Western Emperor)
trump-03-papa-3.Scene: Papa Tre (Pope Three) is the third of the five Papi in the Minchiate Fiorentina — the middle figure of the papal quintet, ranked above the first two Papi in the trump hierarchy. The third Pope bears the vestments and insignia of papal or imperial authority in the 19th-century Florentine engraving tradition.

trump-04-papa-4.name: 4 — Papa Four (the Eastern Emperor)
trump-04-papa-4.Scene: Papa Quattro (Pope Four) is the fourth of the five Papi in the Minchiate Fiorentina — a senior papal or imperial figure whose regalia and authority exceed the first three Papi in the trump ranking. He approaches the apex of the quintet, his vestments and insignia reflecting the increasing solemnity of the higher-ranked Papi.

trump-05-papa-5.name: 5 — Papa Five (Love)
trump-05-papa-5.Scene: Papa Cinque (Pope Five) is the fifth and highest of the five Papi in the Minchiate Fiorentina — the apex of the papal quintet, the most elaborately vested and highest-ranking of the ecclesiastical authority figures that form the Minchiate's distinctive lowest trump sequence. After the five Papi, the trump sequence continues with the Cardinal and Theological Virtues.

trump-06-temperanza.name: 6 — Temperance
trump-06-temperanza.Scene: La Temperanza (Temperance) is the Cardinal Virtue of moderation at trump VI of the Minchiate Fiorentina — depicted as a female figure pouring liquid between two vessels, the conventional allegorical personification of this virtue. The Minchiate places Temperance at VI (immediately above the five Papi), and includes all four Cardinal Virtues in the trump sequence, unlike standard tarot which typically has only three or four.

trump-07-forza.name: 7 — Fortitude
trump-07-forza.Scene: La Forza (Fortitude / Strength) at trump VII of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the Cardinal Virtue of fortitude — depicted as a woman mastering a lion or breaking a column, the conventional allegorical personification. The Minchiate's Forza at VII follows Temperance in the virtues sequence at the base of the higher trump group.

trump-08-giustizia.name: 8 — Justice
trump-08-giustizia.Scene: La Giustizia (Justice) at trump VIII of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the Cardinal Virtue of justice — depicted with sword and scales, the conventional allegorical personification of the balanced measuring of deeds. Justice at VIII in the Minchiate continues the virtues sequence, the sword and scales rendered in the 19th-century Florentine engraving style.

trump-09-ruota.name: 9 — Wheel of Fortune
trump-09-ruota.Scene: La Ruota della Fortuna (The Wheel of Fortune) at trump IX of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows the conventional turning Wheel with ascending and descending figures — the Boethian allegory of Fortune's indifferent rotation. The Wheel follows the four Cardinal Virtues in the Minchiate sequence, placed at IX as the first of the more allegorical trumps above the virtues.

trump-10-carro.name: 10 — The Chariot
trump-10-carro.Scene: Il Carro (The Chariot) at trump X of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a victorious figure in a triumphal vehicle — the Roman triumph allegory at the center of the trump sequence. The Carro at X is the conventional triumphal car image adapted to the Minchiate's expanded trump sequence.

trump-11-gobbo.name: 11 — The Hunchback (Time)
trump-11-gobbo.Scene: Il Gobbo (The Hunchback) at trump XI of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the Minchiate's equivalent of the Hermit — a stooped or hunchbacked elderly figure with a staff, the solitary contemplative recast as a physically marked outsider. 'Gobbo' (hunchback) in Italian street culture was associated with luck, the hunchback's touch being considered fortunate in popular tradition. The Gobbo carries a lantern or staff, his stooped figure rendered in the 19th-century Florentine engraving style.

trump-12-impiccato.name: 12 — The Hanged Man
trump-12-impiccato.Scene: L'Impiccato (The Hanged Man) at trump XII of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a figure suspended by one foot from a gallows — the standard Hanged Man image of the tarot tradition, the figure's expression calm and the suspended posture suggesting willing inversion. The Impiccato at XII in the Minchiate corresponds to the Le Pendu of the Marseille tradition.

trump-13-morte.name: 13 — Death
trump-13-morte.Scene: La Morte (Death) at trump XIII of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows the skeletal figure with scythe cutting through the living — the universal harvester in the conventional allegorical form. In the Minchiate tradition, La Morte at XIII maintains the same position as in the Marseille tarot, the anonymous skeleton who harvests without distinction of rank.

trump-14-diavolo.name: 14 — The Devil
trump-14-diavolo.Scene: Il Diavolo (The Devil) at trump XIV of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows the conventional Devil figure — a winged, horned entity on a pedestal with smaller chained figures below — rendered in the 19th-century Florentine engraving tradition. The Devil at XIV in the Minchiate corresponds to the same position as in many tarot traditions.

trump-15-casa-diavolo.name: 15 — The House of the Devil (Tower)
trump-15-casa-diavolo.Scene: La Casa del Diavolo (The Devil's House) at trump XV of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the Minchiate's version of the Tower card — a structure struck or destroyed, figures falling from the heights. The Minchiate calls this card the Devil's House rather than the Maison-Dieu (God's House) of the Marseille tradition, emphasizing the infernal rather than the divine source of the destruction. The falling figures and ruined structure are rendered in the 19th-century Florentine style.

trump-16-speranza.name: 16 — Hope
trump-16-speranza.Scene: La Speranza (Hope) at trump XVI of the Minchiate Fiorentina is one of the three Theological Virtues unique to the Minchiate and the Cary-Yale among tarot traditions. Hope is depicted as a female figure reaching upward, hands raised toward heaven or holding an anchor (the classical emblem of hope), her gaze directed above the earthly world. La Speranza at XVI continues the expanded virtues sequence of the Minchiate.

trump-17-prudenza.name: 17 — Prudence
trump-17-prudenza.Scene: La Prudenza (Prudence) at trump XVII of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the fourth Cardinal Virtue — the only one absent from most standard tarot decks (which typically include only Temperance, Fortitude, and Justice). The Minchiate's inclusion of Prudence at XVII makes it one of only two tarot traditions to include all four Cardinal Virtues. Prudence is depicted with mirror and serpent, the classical attributes of foresight and self-knowledge.

trump-18-fede.name: 18 — Faith
trump-18-fede.Scene: La Fede (Faith) at trump XVIII of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the second Theological Virtue in the Minchiate sequence — depicted as a female figure with cross, chalice, or Apostles' Creed scroll, her gaze directed upward toward what cannot be seen. Faith at XVIII in the Minchiate's expanded trump sequence represents the belief that exceeds evidence.

trump-19-carita.name: 19 — Charity
trump-19-carita.Scene: La Carità (Charity) at trump XIX of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the third and highest Theological Virtue — depicted as a woman giving, nurturing children at her breast, or holding her heart toward others. The greatest of the three theological virtues according to Paul's Corinthians, Charity is positioned at XIX just before the elemental trumps that begin at XX.

trump-20-fuoco.name: 20 — Fire
trump-20-fuoco.Scene: Il Fuoco (Fire) at trump XX of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the first of the four Elemental trumps — a unique feature of the Minchiate not found in standard tarot. Fire is depicted as a flame, a salamander (the mythical fire-creature), or a blazing brazier, the element in its conventional allegorical or symbolic form. The four elements (Fire, Water, Earth, Air at XX-XXIII) are a cosmological layer added to the Minchiate's already extended trump sequence.

trump-21-acqua.name: 21 — Water
trump-21-acqua.Scene: L'Acqua (Water) at trump XXI of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the second elemental trump — depicted as waves, a water-bearer, or a figure associated with the flowing, receptive, and deep qualities of the water element. L'Acqua at XXI continues the four-element cosmological sequence unique to the Minchiate.

trump-22-terra.name: 22 — Earth
trump-22-terra.Scene: La Terra (Earth) at trump XXII of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the third elemental trump — depicted as a figure of earthly stability, a globe, or an agricultural or geological symbol. La Terra at XXII represents the stable, material, and productive element in the Minchiate's cosmological trump sequence.

trump-23-aria.name: 23 — Air
trump-23-aria.Scene: L'Aria (Air) at trump XXIII of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the fourth and final elemental trump — depicted as a figure of the atmosphere, a windblown form, or an angel or bird associated with the aerial element. L'Aria at XXIII completes the four-element cosmological sequence that distinguishes the Minchiate from all standard tarot traditions.

trump-24-bilancia.name: 24 — Libra
trump-24-bilancia.Scene: La Bilancia (Libra / The Scales) at trump XXIV of the Minchiate Fiorentina is the first of 12 zodiac trumps — a unique feature of the Minchiate that adds the entire zodiacal sequence to its extended trump hierarchy. Libra is depicted as a female figure with scales, the astrological sign rendered as an allegorical figure or as the zodiacal symbol. The 12 zodiac trumps (XXIV-XXXV) form the most astronomically comprehensive layer of the Minchiate's 40-trump sequence.

trump-25-vergine.name: 25 — Virgo
trump-25-vergine.Scene: La Vergine (Virgo / The Virgin) at trump XXV of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Virgo — a female figure representing purity, discernment, and the harvest of the earth. The Vergine is shown in the allegorical style of 19th-century Florentine engraving, the astrological sign rendered as a personified figure.

trump-26-scorpione.name: 26 — Scorpio
trump-26-scorpione.Scene: Il Scorpione (Scorpio) at trump XXVI of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Scorpio — a figure associated with the scorpion, intensity, hidden depths, and transformation. The Scorpione is shown in the allegorical style of the 19th-century Florentine edition, the water sign rendered as a figure or accompanied by the scorpion emblem.

trump-27-ariete.name: 27 — Aries
trump-27-ariete.Scene: L'Ariete (Aries / The Ram) at trump XXVII of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Aries — a figure with a ram or wearing ram's horns, the first sign of the zodiac associated with the fiery beginning of the astrological year. The Ariete continues the Minchiate's unique zodiacal trump sequence.

trump-28-capricorno.name: 28 — Capricorn
trump-28-capricorno.Scene: Il Capricorno (Capricorn) at trump XXVIII of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Capricorn — the sea-goat or mountain-goat figure associated with ambition, discipline, and the earth element. The Capricorno continues the Minchiate's unique zodiacal sequence in the 19th-century Florentine engraving style.

trump-29-sagittario.name: 29 — Sagittarius
trump-29-sagittario.Scene: Il Sagittario (Sagittarius) at trump XXIX of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Sagittarius — the archer or centaur-archer figure associated with philosophical expansion, adventure, and the fiery quest for truth. The Sagittario continues the Minchiate's zodiacal sequence.

trump-30-cancro.name: 30 — Cancer
trump-30-cancro.Scene: Il Cancro (Cancer) at trump XXX of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Cancer — the crab figure associated with home, emotional depth, and the nurturing of what is vulnerable. The Cancro is shown in the allegorical style of the 1860-1890 Florentine edition.

trump-31-pesci.name: 31 — Pisces
trump-31-pesci.Scene: I Pesci (Pisces) at trump XXXI of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Pisces — two fish swimming in opposite directions, associated with compassion, dissolving boundaries, and the deep waters of the unconscious. The Pesci is shown as two fish or as a figure associated with the dual fish symbol.

trump-32-acquario.name: 32 — Aquarius
trump-32-acquario.Scene: L'Acquario (Aquarius) at trump XXXII of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Aquarius — the water-bearer pouring from a vessel, associated with innovation, community, and the distribution of what flows. The Acquario is shown as a figure pouring water, the air sign represented through the paradox of the water-bearer.

trump-33-leone.name: 33 — Leo
trump-33-leone.Scene: Il Leone (Leo) at trump XXXIII of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Leo — the lion figure associated with creative expression, confidence, and solar energy. The Leone is shown as a lion or as a figure with lion attributes, the fire sign of leadership and creative authority.

trump-34-toro.name: 34 — Taurus
trump-34-toro.Scene: Il Toro (Taurus) at trump XXXIV of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Taurus — the bull figure associated with earthy sensuality, stability, and the patient accumulation of material resources. The Toro is shown as a bull or as a figure with bull attributes, the earth sign of physical pleasure and endurance.

trump-35-gemelli.name: 35 — Gemini
trump-35-gemelli.Scene: I Gemelli (Gemini) at trump XXXV of the Minchiate Fiorentina depicts the zodiacal sign of Gemini — two figures or twins associated with intellectual duality, communication, and the capacity to hold opposing perspectives simultaneously. The Gemelli is shown as two figures or twins, the air sign of versatile mental energy.

trump-36-stella.name: 36 — The Star
trump-36-stella.Scene: La Stella (The Star) at trump XXXVI of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows the conventional Star card image — a nude or draped female figure pouring water beneath a large central star surrounded by smaller stars. After the 12 zodiac trumps, the celestial sequence of Star, Moon, Sun, and World begins. The Stella at XXXVI follows the Marseille Star's iconographic type in the 19th-century Florentine engraving style.

trump-37-luna.name: 37 — The Moon
trump-37-luna.Scene: La Luna (The Moon) at trump XXXVII of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows the Moon card image — a moon face in the sky above baying dogs or wolves, with a pool and a crayfish. The Luna at XXXVII follows the Marseille Moon's iconographic type in the 19th-century Florentine style, the distorting nocturnal light placed in the penultimate celestial group.

trump-38-sole.name: 38 — The Sun
trump-38-sole.Scene: Il Sole (The Sun) at trump XXXVIII of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows the Sun card image — a large solar face radiating rays over two children playing in sunlight. The Sole at XXXVIII is the penultimate trump before the World (XXXIX) and the Last Judgment (XL), the joyful solar consciousness that precedes the deck's cosmic completion.

trump-39-mondo.name: 39 — The World
trump-39-mondo.Scene: Il Mondo (The World) at trump XXXIX of the Minchiate Fiorentina shows the World card image — a female figure dancing within a laurel mandorla surrounded by the four zodiacal beings at the corners. The Mondo at XXXIX is the penultimate numbered trump, placed just before the Trombe (Last Judgment) at XL — a reversal of the Marseille sequence where Judgment typically precedes the World.

trump-40-trombe.name: 40 — The Trumpets (Fame / Judgement)
trump-40-trombe.Scene: Le Trombe (The Trumpets / Last Judgment) at trump XL — the highest-ranking trump of the Minchiate Fiorentina — shows the angel or angels with trumpets summoning the risen dead. In the Minchiate, the Last Judgment is the apex trump (XL), the highest and most powerful card in the deck's hierarchy, ranking above even the World (XXXIX). The Trombe are rendered as sounding trumpets of divine judgment calling all things to account at the end of time.

batons-ace.name: Ace of Batons
batons-ace.Scene: The Ace of Batons in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a single knotted staff or club — the concentrated emblem of the fiery creative suit. The Minchiate's pip cards follow the Italian playing card convention of geometric suit symbol arrangement.

batons-02.name: Two of Batons
batons-02.Scene: Two baton pips in bilateral arrangement — the suit's first division, two clubs in geometric symmetry.

batons-03.name: Three of Batons
batons-03.Scene: Three baton pips in triangular arrangement — the suit at three.

batons-04.name: Four of Batons
batons-04.Scene: Four baton pips in square arrangement — the stable quadrant of the suit.

batons-05.name: Five of Batons
batons-05.Scene: Five baton pips in quincunx or asymmetric arrangement — the mid-point disruption.

batons-06.name: Six of Batons
batons-06.Scene: Six baton pips in even rows — the balanced creative abundance at six.

batons-07.name: Seven of Batons
batons-07.Scene: Seven baton pips in asymmetric arrangement — the patient threshold at seven.

batons-08.name: Eight of Batons
batons-08.Scene: Eight baton pips in orderly pairs — the competent creative doubling at eight.

batons-09.name: Nine of Batons
batons-09.Scene: Nine baton pips in the three-by-three square — near-completion at nine.

batons-10.name: Ten of Batons
batons-10.Scene: Ten baton pips in the final arrangement — the complete creative expression.

batons-jack.name: Jack of Batons
batons-jack.Scene: The Fante di Bastoni (Jack/Knave of Batons) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a young male figure in standing pose bearing the club or staff — the youngest male court rank of the suit, a page or footman of the creative fire. In the Minchiate court tradition, the Fante is the lowest court rank, often shown as a standing figure in Italian costume of the period.

batons-knight.name: Knight of Batons
batons-knight.Scene: The Cavaliere/Cavallo di Bastoni (Knight of Batons) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a mounted figure bearing the club or staff, his horse in an active posture. The mounted court figure in the Minchiate follows the Italian playing card convention of showing the knight on horseback.

batons-queen.name: Queen of Batons
batons-queen.Scene: La Regina di Bastoni (Queen of Batons) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a crowned female figure seated or standing, bearing the club or staff as the emblem of her suit's authority. The Queen court figure in the Minchiate follows the Italian playing card convention.

batons-king.name: King of Batons
batons-king.Scene: Il Re di Bastoni (King of Batons) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a crowned male figure seated or standing, bearing the club or staff as the emblem of his suit's authority. The King is the apex of the suit's court hierarchy in the Minchiate tradition.

coins-ace.name: Ace of Coins
coins-ace.Scene: The Ace of Coins in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a single large coin or disc — the concentrated emblem of the material and earthly suit. The Minchiate pip cards follow the Italian playing card geometric arrangement tradition.

coins-02.name: Two of Coins
coins-02.Scene: Two coin pips in bilateral arrangement — the suit's first division.

coins-03.name: Three of Coins
coins-03.Scene: Three coin pips in triangular arrangement — the material triad.

coins-04.name: Four of Coins
coins-04.Scene: Four coin pips in square arrangement — the stable material quadrant.

coins-05.name: Five of Coins
coins-05.Scene: Five coin pips in quincunx arrangement — the mid-point material disruption.

coins-06.name: Six of Coins
coins-06.Scene: Six coin pips in even rows — the balanced material abundance at six.

coins-07.name: Seven of Coins
coins-07.Scene: Seven coin pips in asymmetric arrangement — the patient material threshold.

coins-08.name: Eight of Coins
coins-08.Scene: Eight coin pips in orderly pairs — the competent material doubling at eight.

coins-09.name: Nine of Coins
coins-09.Scene: Nine coin pips in the three-by-three square — material near-completion.

coins-10.name: Ten of Coins
coins-10.Scene: Ten coin pips in the final arrangement — the complete material expression.

coins-jack.name: Jack of Coins
coins-jack.Scene: The Fante di Denari (Jack/Knave of Coins) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a young standing male figure bearing the coin — the youngest male court rank of the material suit, an attentive student of practical matters in the Italian court tradition.

coins-knight.name: Knight of Coins
coins-knight.Scene: The Cavaliere/Cavallo di Denari (Knight of Coins) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a mounted male figure bearing the coin, his horse in a methodical or walking posture — the most patient of the mounted court figures, deliberate in his material pursuit.

coins-queen.name: Queen of Coins
coins-queen.Scene: La Regina di Denari (Queen of Coins) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a crowned female figure bearing the coin as the emblem of her suit's authority — the high feminine authority of the material suit, practical generosity and stewardship.

coins-king.name: King of Coins
coins-king.Scene: Il Re di Denari (King of Coins) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a crowned male figure bearing the coin as the emblem of his apex authority — the master of earthly resources and practical competence.

cups-ace.name: Ace of Cups
cups-ace.Scene: The Ace of Cups in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a single ornate chalice or vase — the concentrated emblem of the emotional and spiritual suit. The Minchiate pip cards follow the Italian playing card convention of geometric suit symbol arrangement.

cups-02.name: Two of Cups
cups-02.Scene: Two cup pips in bilateral arrangement — the emotional dyad.

cups-03.name: Three of Cups
cups-03.Scene: Three cup pips in triangular arrangement — the communal emotional triad.

cups-04.name: Four of Cups
cups-04.Scene: Four cup pips in square arrangement — the stable emotional quadrant.

cups-05.name: Five of Cups
cups-05.Scene: Five cup pips in quincunx arrangement — the emotional mid-point disruption.

cups-06.name: Six of Cups
cups-06.Scene: Six cup pips in even rows — the balanced emotional abundance at six.

cups-07.name: Seven of Cups
cups-07.Scene: Seven cup pips in asymmetric arrangement — the emotional threshold at seven.

cups-08.name: Eight of Cups
cups-08.Scene: Eight cup pips in orderly pairs — the emotional competence at eight.

cups-09.name: Nine of Cups
cups-09.Scene: Nine cup pips in the three-by-three square — emotional near-completion.

cups-10.name: Ten of Cups
cups-10.Scene: Ten cup pips in the final arrangement — the complete emotional expression.

cups-jack.name: Jack of Cups
cups-jack.Scene: The Fante di Coppe (Jack/Knave of Cups) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a young standing male figure bearing the cup — the youngest male court rank of the emotional suit, imaginative and receptive in the Italian court tradition.

cups-knight.name: Knight of Cups
cups-knight.Scene: The Cavaliere/Cavallo di Coppe (Knight of Cups) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a mounted male figure bearing the cup, his horse in a gentle forward-stepping posture — the romantic messenger of the emotional suit carrying his offering on horseback.

cups-queen.name: Queen of Cups
cups-queen.Scene: La Regina di Coppe (Queen of Cups) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a crowned female figure bearing the cup as the emblem of her suit's authority — the high feminine authority of the emotional suit, deep feeling and compassionate understanding.

cups-king.name: King of Cups
cups-king.Scene: Il Re di Coppe (King of Cups) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a crowned male figure bearing the cup as the emblem of his apex authority — the master of emotional maturity and wisdom in feeling.

swords-ace.name: Ace of Swords
swords-ace.Scene: The Ace of Swords in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a single upright sword or blade — the concentrated emblem of the mental and martial suit. The Minchiate pip cards follow the Italian playing card convention of geometric suit symbol arrangement.

swords-02.name: Two of Swords
swords-02.Scene: Two sword pips crossed or in bilateral arrangement — the mental dyad in tension.

swords-03.name: Three of Swords
swords-03.Scene: Three sword pips in triangular arrangement — the mental triad.

swords-04.name: Four of Swords
swords-04.Scene: Four sword pips in cross arrangement — the stable mental quadrant.

swords-05.name: Five of Swords
swords-05.Scene: Five sword pips in asymmetric arrangement — the disruptive mid-point.

swords-06.name: Six of Swords
swords-06.Scene: Six sword pips in even rows — the balanced mental arrangement at six.

swords-07.name: Seven of Swords
swords-07.Scene: Seven sword pips in asymmetric arrangement — the strategic threshold at seven.

swords-08.name: Eight of Swords
swords-08.Scene: Eight sword pips in orderly pairs — the even doubling of mental resources.

swords-09.name: Nine of Swords
swords-09.Scene: Nine sword pips in the three-by-three square — mental near-completion.

swords-10.name: Ten of Swords
swords-10.Scene: Ten sword pips in the final arrangement — the complete mental expression.

swords-jack.name: Jack of Swords
swords-jack.Scene: The Fante di Spade (Jack/Knave of Swords) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a young standing male figure bearing the sword — the youngest male court rank of the mental suit, vigilant and alert in the Italian court tradition.

swords-knight.name: Knight of Swords
swords-knight.Scene: The Cavaliere/Cavallo di Spade (Knight of Swords) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a mounted male figure with sword raised, his horse in a charging or dynamic posture — the most decisive and swift of the mounted court figures, the blade of action in motion.

swords-queen.name: Queen of Swords
swords-queen.Scene: La Regina di Spade (Queen of Swords) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a crowned female figure bearing the sword — the high feminine authority of the mental suit, clarity and independent perception forged through experience.

swords-king.name: King of Swords
swords-king.Scene: Il Re di Spade (King of Swords) in the Minchiate Fiorentina shows a crowned male figure bearing the sword as the emblem of his apex authority — the master of intellectual command and clear judgment.

emg-papi.name: The Five Papi
emg-papi.Scene: The five Papi (Popes) are the most distinctive innovation of the Minchiate Fiorentina — occupying trump positions I through V, replacing the standard tarot's Papess, Pope, Emperor, Empress, and Lovers with a sequence of five papal or imperial authority figures. The Papi are the weakest trumps in the Minchiate hierarchy, the base of the 40-trump sequence, a quintet of figures that reflects the Florentine political context of the 16th century in which the Minchiate emerged.

emg-virtues.name: The Seven Virtues — Complete
emg-virtues.Scene: The Virtues of the Minchiate Fiorentina form the most comprehensive virtue sequence in any tarot tradition — four Cardinal Virtues (Temperance at VI, Fortitude at VII, Justice at VIII, Prudence at XVII) and three Theological Virtues (Hope at XVI, Faith at XVIII, Charity at XIX), totaling seven virtue trumps. No other surviving tarot includes all four Cardinal Virtues alongside the three Theological Virtues. The Minchiate's virtue sequence reflects the Florentine humanist and Christian tradition that produced this deck.

emg-elements.name: The Four Elements
emg-elements.Scene: The four Elements (Fire at XX, Water at XXI, Earth at XXII, Air at XXIII) form a unique cosmological group in the Minchiate Fiorentina — a layer of elemental trumps not found in any standard tarot tradition. The elements are placed after the Virtues and before the Zodiac signs, creating a cosmological sequence that expands the Minchiate's trump hierarchy to encompass the entire classical worldview: moral virtues, cosmic elements, astronomical signs, and celestial completion.

emg-zodiac.name: The Twelve Signs of the Zodiac
emg-zodiac.Scene: The twelve Zodiac signs (Libra at XXIV through Gemini at XXXV) form the largest single group in the Minchiate Fiorentina's unique trump sequence — twelve consecutive trumps representing the astrological signs of the zodiac, from Libra to Gemini. No other tarot tradition includes the complete zodiacal sequence as a group of trump cards. The zodiac trumps occupy the center of the Minchiate's 40-trump hierarchy, placed between the elemental layer and the final celestial sequence.

emg-arie.name: The Arie — The Five Supreme Cards
emg-arie.Scene: The final celestial sequence of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the Star (XXXVI), Moon (XXXVII), Sun (XXXVIII), World (XXXIX), and Last Judgment / Trumpets (XL) — forms the apex group of the 40-trump hierarchy. These five cards parallel the standard tarot's final celestial group but with the Last Judgment placed highest (at XL) rather than the World, a distinctive Minchiate innovation that places the divine summons above the cosmic completion.

emg-suit-batons.name: Suit of Batons (Bastoni) — Fire
emg-suit-batons.Scene: The batons suit of the Minchiate Fiorentina comprises Ace through 10 pip cards and four court ranks (Jack/Fante, Knight/Cavaliere, Queen/Regina, King/Re), totaling 14 cards. The batons suit of the Minchiate follows the Italian playing card convention of knotted clubs or staffs in geometric pip arrangements.

emg-suit-coins.name: Suit of Coins (Denari) — Earth
emg-suit-coins.Scene: The coins suit of the Minchiate Fiorentina comprises Ace through 10 pip cards and four court ranks, totaling 14 cards. The coins suit follows the Italian playing card convention of round disc pips in geometric arrangements.

emg-suit-cups.name: Suit of Cups (Coppe) — Water
emg-suit-cups.Scene: The cups suit of the Minchiate Fiorentina comprises Ace through 10 pip cards and four court ranks, totaling 14 cards. The cups suit follows the Italian playing card convention of ornate chalice pips in geometric arrangements.

emg-suit-swords.name: Suit of Swords (Spade) — Air
emg-suit-swords.Scene: The swords suit of the Minchiate Fiorentina comprises Ace through 10 pip cards and four court ranks, totaling 14 cards. The swords suit follows the Italian playing card convention of blade pips in geometric arrangements.

kw-minchiate.name: Minchiate
kw-minchiate.Scene: A keyword grouping identifying all items belonging to the Minchiate Fiorentina — the expanded 97-card Florentine game deck that added 19 extra trumps to the standard tarot's 22, creating a 41-trump sequence. The Minchiate originated in Florence in the 16th century (attributed variously to Leonardo da Vinci or the 1530s Florentine gaming culture) and remained popular in Florence and Tuscany until the 19th century. This edition dates to 1860-1890.

kw-trionfi.name: Trionfi
kw-trionfi.Scene: A keyword grouping for the trionfi (triumphs) — the 41 trump cards of the Minchiate Fiorentina, from Il Matto (0) through Le Trombe (40). The term 'trionfi' refers to the Roman triumph tradition that gave tarot its name, the allegorical procession of triumphal figures that constitutes the tarot's major arcana.

kw-minor.name: Minor
kw-minor.Scene: A keyword grouping for all 56 minor arcana cards of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the four suits of 14 cards each. In the Minchiate game, the minor arcana are lower in rank than any of the 41 trumps, the suit cards forming the base of the game hierarchy.

kw-court.name: Court
kw-court.Scene: A keyword grouping for all 16 court cards across the four suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the Fante (Jack), Cavaliere (Knight), Regina (Queen), and Re (King) of each suit. The Minchiate courts use the four-rank Italian playing card system with the Fante as the lowest rank.

kw-air.name: Air
kw-air.Scene: A keyword grouping for items associated with Air — both the elemental trump L'Aria (XXIII) and the swords suit, which is traditionally associated with the air element.

kw-earth.name: Earth
kw-earth.Scene: A keyword grouping for items associated with Earth — both the elemental trump La Terra (XXII) and the coins suit, traditionally associated with the earth element.

kw-fire.name: Fire
kw-fire.Scene: A keyword grouping for items associated with Fire — both the elemental trump Il Fuoco (XX) and the batons suit, traditionally associated with the fire element.

kw-water.name: Water
kw-water.Scene: A keyword grouping for items associated with Water — both the elemental trump L'Acqua (XXI) and the cups suit, traditionally associated with the water element.

kw-batons.name: Batons
kw-batons.Scene: A keyword grouping for the batons suit of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the knotted club suit of creative fire.

kw-coins.name: Coins
kw-coins.Scene: A keyword grouping for the coins suit of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the disc suit of material resources.

kw-cups.name: Cups
kw-cups.Scene: A keyword grouping for the cups suit of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the chalice suit of emotional depth.

kw-swords.name: Swords
kw-swords.Scene: A keyword grouping for the swords suit of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the blade suit of mental clarity.

kw-zodiac.name: Zodiac
kw-zodiac.Scene: A keyword grouping for the 12 zodiac trump cards of the Minchiate Fiorentina (trumps XXIV-XXXV: Libra, Virgo, Scorpio, Aries, Capricorn, Sagittarius, Cancer, Pisces, Aquarius, Leo, Taurus, Gemini). The zodiacal sequence is the largest unique group in the Minchiate's expanded trump hierarchy, a complete 12-sign astrological cycle rendered as consecutive trump cards.

kw-bastoni.name: Bastoni
kw-bastoni.Scene: The Italian name 'Bastoni' for the batons suit in the Minchiate tradition.

kw-coppe.name: Coppe
kw-coppe.Scene: The Italian name 'Coppe' for the cups suit in the Minchiate tradition.

kw-denari.name: Denari
kw-denari.Scene: The Italian name 'Denari' for the coins suit in the Minchiate tradition.

kw-spade.name: Spade
kw-spade.Scene: The Italian name 'Spade' for the swords suit in the Minchiate tradition.

kw-trump.name: Trump
kw-trump.Scene: A keyword grouping for all 41 trump cards of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the trionfi from Il Matto through Le Trombe.

kw-virtue.name: Virtue
kw-virtue.Scene: A keyword grouping for the seven Virtue trump cards of the Minchiate Fiorentina — four Cardinal Virtues (Temperance VI, Fortitude VII, Justice VIII, Prudence XVII) and three Theological Virtues (Hope XVI, Faith XVIII, Charity XIX). The Minchiate's complete virtue sequence is unique among tarot traditions.

kw-arie.name: Arie
kw-arie.Scene: The Italian name 'Arie' (plural of 'aria' in the musical sense, or referring to 'Aria/Air') for the final celestial group of the Minchiate — the Star, Moon, Sun, World, and Trumpets that form the apex of the 40-trump hierarchy.

kw-papi.name: Papi
kw-papi.Scene: A keyword grouping for the five Papi trump cards (I-V) of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the unique sequence of papal/imperial figures that replaces the standard tarot's Papess, Pope, Emperor, Empress, and Lovers. The Papi are the weakest of the 40 numbered trumps.

kw-ace.name: Ace
kw-ace.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four aces across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina — the concentrated seeds of each suit.

kw-cavallo.name: Cavallo
kw-cavallo.Scene: The Italian name 'Cavallo' (horse) for the Knight court rank in the Minchiate tradition — the mounted court figure in Italian playing card nomenclature.

kw-eight.name: Eight
kw-eight.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four eight-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-element.name: Element
kw-element.Scene: A keyword grouping for the four elemental trump cards of the Minchiate Fiorentina — Fire (XX), Water (XXI), Earth (XXII), and Air (XXIII). These four consecutive trumps constitute a unique cosmological layer not found in any standard tarot tradition.

kw-fante.name: Fante
kw-fante.Scene: The Italian name 'Fante' (foot soldier, page) for the Jack court rank in the Minchiate tradition — the youngest and lowest male court figure in Italian playing card nomenclature.

kw-five.name: Five
kw-five.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four five-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-four.name: Four
kw-four.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four four-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-jack.name: Jack
kw-jack.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four Jack (Fante) court figures across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-king.name: King
kw-king.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four King (Re) court figures across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-knight.name: Knight
kw-knight.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four Knight (Cavaliere) court figures across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-nine.name: Nine
kw-nine.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four nine-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-queen.name: Queen
kw-queen.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four Queen (Regina) court figures across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-re.name: Re
kw-re.Scene: The Italian name 'Re' (king) for the King court rank in the Minchiate tradition — the apex male court figure in Italian playing card nomenclature.

kw-regina.name: Regina
kw-regina.Scene: The Italian name 'Regina' (queen) for the Queen court rank in the Minchiate tradition — the high female court figure in Italian playing card nomenclature.

kw-seven.name: Seven
kw-seven.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four seven-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-six.name: Six
kw-six.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four six-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-ten.name: Ten
kw-ten.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four ten-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-three.name: Three
kw-three.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four three-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

kw-two.name: Two
kw-two.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four two-pip cards across the suits of the Minchiate Fiorentina.

axis-keyword.name: By Keyword
axis-keyword.Scene: The keyword axis of the Minchiate Fiorentina organizes the deck's 147 items by thematic grouping — the unique categories of the Minchiate (Papi, Virtues, Elements, Zodiac, celestial sequence), the four suits and their pip numbers, court ranks in Italian and English, and elemental associations. This axis allows navigation across the most expanded tarot tradition through the conceptual patterns that structure its 41 trumps and 56 minor arcana.
